title: Encrypt Secret Service password transport before release
description: Replace the plain Secret Service session used by the collection client with GNOME's supported dh-ietf1024-sha256-aes128-cbc-pkcs7 session before publishing. Keep direct zbus control of the private GNOME interface while deriving the session AES key, generating a fresh IV per Secret, and sending ciphertext rather than collection passwords through the D-Bus broker. Plain-session CLI work may proceed as an MVP, but this is a release blocker.
acceptance_criteria: Blocking collection operations negotiate the encrypted session and the future async/Tokio adapter can reuse the session model; private-broker Rust proof covers list/unlock/change with encrypted Secret tuples; a private-bus monitor proves password bytes do not appear in password-method message bodies; keys, IV plaintext buffers, and owned ciphertext/plaintext intermediates use best-effort zeroization where supported; no silent fallback to plain occurs without an explicit documented policy; README removes the MVP cleartext warning only after proof; full checks pass.
notes:
Slice 1 (sans-I/O crypto core) implemented in src/secret_service/session.rs, commit 52bfa653.

- ClientKeypair::generate()/public_key()/derive_aes_key(&[u8]) -> SessionKey; seal(&SessionKey, &[u8]) -> SealedSecret{iv, ciphertext}. No zbus or I/O types in the module; reusable verbatim by the async adapter.
- Protocol per verified spec: RFC 2409 1024-bit MODP prime pinned byte-for-byte to egg/egg-dh.c (test transcribes the hex); peer key must be 1..=128 bytes and 1 < y < p-1; shared secret left-padded to 128 bytes before HKDF-SHA256(empty salt, empty info, L=16); AES-128-CBC + PKCS7 with fresh per-Secret IV.
- Deps added: crypto-bigint 0.7 (alloc,zeroize), sha2 0.11 + hkdf 0.13, aes 0.9 (zeroize) + cbc 0.2 (zeroize) [aes-cbc crate no longer published; cbc+aes is its successor], getrandom 0.4.
- Modpow uses crypto-bigint BoxedUint::pow_mod (Montgomery ladder, constant-time in the fresh per-session exponent); vartime cmp used only on public peer data with documented rationale.
- Zeroization: private exponent (Zeroizing<BoxedUint>), shared secret, 128-byte ikm buffer, AES key, IV, and padded plaintext all zeroizing; SessionKey/ClientKeypair/SealedSecret.iv carry no Debug/Clone/Display.
- Tests: 96 passed / 4 skipped (baseline 85/4, strictly additive). Prime pin, RFC 5869 A.1-A.3 via the exact hkdf helper, egg/test-dh.c-style both-sides agreement, Python-computed fixed KAT (x,y,X,Y,ikm,key), two left-pad KATs proving 128-byte normalization changes the key (3 and 625), peer-key rejection (empty,0,1,p-1,p,>128B,0xff..ff), seal shape/fresh-IV/boundary/round-trip/wrong-key. clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, cargo doc warning-free.
- KAT generator script retained at ~/tmp-opencode/gmell_kat.py (provenance).

No zbus/blocking.rs changes in this slice; slice 2 will wire open_session + seal into blocking.rs.
Slice 2 (wiring + real-daemon proof) done, commits 6d4ef8e9 (wiring) and 0c9298e5 (monitors/proofs).

WIRING: BlockingClient::new negotiates dh-ietf1024-sha256-aes128-cbc-pkcs7 (public key as the ay variant; daemon requires G_VARIANT_TYPE_BYTESTRING after its own unwrap — confirmed against gkd-secret-session.c and live daemon). decode_open_session_output decodes the reply (u8-array Value; zvariant 5 has no ByteArray variant); derive via session core; both call sites seal with fresh IVs; AlreadyUnlocked early return unchanged. Error mapping per review decisions: Error::EncryptedSessionUnsupported (org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NotSupported from open_session; no plain fallback — deliberate divergence from libsecret) and Error::Session(CryptoError); both exit 1, no new exit code.

INTEROP FINDINGS (live daemon 48.0): handshake succeeded first run — variant shape, minimal big-endian public key, left-pad normalization, HKDF, and seal are all correct as implemented. The daemon performs NO client-public-key validation (accepted a 3-byte probe key); our validator stays strict. Empty ay renders as 'ARRAY "y" {' with no BYTE lines in busctl monitor, which the plain-shape detector relies on.

MONITOR: new BodyMonitor (busctl monitor, streaming pipe, never on disk) scans every raw line (literal+hex) and every reconstructed zeroized ay run (the only place a plaintext password can hide in a BYTE-decimal rendering) for all generated passwords = ABSENCE; verdicts per password-method arity 16-byte-IV + 16-multiple ciphertext = PRESENCE (plain secret's empty IV fails); OpenSession monitor verdicts the DH algorithm string (plain negotiation fails closed). Retained artifacts: header/length/verdict summaries only; readiness logs secret-scanned and deleted. Fixture now negotiates encrypted too (shared core), so fixture CreateWithMasterPassword bodies are also ciphertext.

PROOF RESULTS: rust-broker 1/1 (2 creates, 6 unlocks, 1 change all encrypted; 2 DH negotiations), rust-cli 1/1 (11 unlocks, 3 changes cross-checked vs header monitor, negotiations == invocations+1 all DH), rust-nextest 2/2, broker 7/7+probe, ordinary nextest 106 passed / 4 skipped (baseline skips unchanged), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, cargo doc warning-free. dev/harness/check all passes.

Remaining for slice 3: docs/status/README updates (remove MVP cleartext warning), maintained evidence doc, close recommendation.
Slice 3 (documentation, evidence, closure) done, commits 3247fb73 (README+status) and 42d5c4c4 (evidence+guide).

'Blocking collection operations negotiate the encrypted session and the future async/Tokio adapter can reuse the session model' — SATISFIED: every BlockingClient connection negotiates dh-ietf1024-sha256-aes128-cbc-pkcs7; src/secret_service/session.rs is sans-I/O (no zbus/I/O types) and consumed verbatim by both the product client and the test fixture; status.md records the reuse path.

5. 'no silent fallback to plain occurs without an explicit documented policy' — SATISFIED: no fallback exists at all; documented as a durable decision in status.md and in the EncryptedSessionUnsupported error (deliberate divergence from libsecret).
6. 'README removes the MVP cleartext warning only after proof' — SATISFIED: warning replaced with the encrypted-session statement citing doc/harness/session0.gpt6a.md, after the monitor proof landed.

title: Prove multi-collection private D-Bus unlock/change under the broker harness
description: Executable proof that the committed Rust zbus client (BlockingClient) handles multiple GNOME collections with different passwords by stable CollectionId, under dev/harness/broker.py isolation. Fixture setup only may call the private CreateWithMasterPassword and standard Lock methods on disposable collections. This ticket records evidence for gmell-dbus-collections; it does not duplicate or implement product features, CLI wiring, or control-code retirement.
acceptance_criteria: An ignored Rust integration test runs only via the private broker harness and a new explicit dev/harness/check mode that fails hard (125) on missing broker/systemd/journal/daemon/monitor prerequisites. Two persistent disposable collections are created with distinguishable labels and distinct random passwords (never printed or logged). Through BlockingClient: both IDs list with correct labels; already-unlocked unlock returns AlreadyUnlocked leaving lock state false without relocking or verifying; after fixture-only locking, wrong password is PasswordDenied while locked and each distinct password unlocks only its own collection; a missing ID returns CollectionNotFound; change_password A->A2 succeeds and after fixture-only lock A is denied while A2 unlocks. Wire evidence proves ordinary unlock emits no standard Lock method call: a match-filtered private-bus monitor attributes every org.freedesktop.Secret.Service.Lock call to the fixture connection. Every retained proof artifact is scanned for generated secret bytes; owned Rust buffers are zeroized. Evidence doc records commands, lock-state transitions, no-relock evidence, and the plain-session/D-Bus-copy zeroization limit honestly.

title: Implement collection-targeted GNOME D-Bus backend
description: Prove and implement a collection-oriented client using standard Secret Service discovery plus GNOME's private InternalUnsupportedGuiltRiddenInterface master-password methods. Generate both blocking and async-capable zbus proxies from one interface declaration; expose the blocking adapter now without preventing a future Tokio adapter. Open a Secret Service session, list collection object paths and labels/lock state, unlock one selected existing collection with its own password, and classify wrong-password, missing-collection, unavailable-service, and unsupported-private-interface errors. Master means collection password only. Never lock/relock as part of ordinary unlock.
acceptance_criteria: Against an isolated private-bus daemon, the client lists at least login and a second collection by stable ID, unlocks each with different passwords, rejects a wrong password while the target is locked, reports missing collections, and leaves an already-unlocked collection unlocked without password verification or relocking. Unit/proxy tests cover wire signatures and error mapping without touching the real session bus. Blocking API is implemented; generated proxy/interface machinery remains usable by a future async/Tokio adapter. No secret value is Debug/logged. README corrects the prior only-control-socket claim only after proof.
notes:
User approved zbus-only collection architecture with IDs plus list. Default unlock must never relock to verify a password; any future verification mode must be explicit and warn about lock side effects. First checkpoint proves the private D-Bus method against an isolated daemon before control transport retirement.

title: Provide required private-broker harness
description: Implement the required private dbus-broker-backed harness topology for the approved zbus-only collection architecture. Preserve the control-only harness as a sibling mode, but provide a reusable isolated-bus command lifecycle that manually launches gnome-keyring-daemon, loads no host service activation directories, and never exposes the real user bus.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable command mode creates a unique private broker socket with a minimal no-activation configuration, manually launches gnome-keyring-daemon, and exports the explicit private DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS while preserving HOME/XDG/storage isolation. Bounded readiness proves the bus answers and the daemon owns org.gnome.keyring and org.freedesktop.secrets. A focused probe opens a plain Secret Service session and confirms org.gnome.keyring.InternalUnsupportedGuiltRiddenInterface is introspectable or callable without touching the real bus. Exact launcher, broker, daemon, and command processes are owned and reaped under bounded TERM/KILL deadlines with redacted, parallel-safe evidence. Documentation reproduces inherited socket activation, successful --scope system, --scope user ENOMEDIUM, journal/systemd dependencies, and the configuration/session-isolation boundary. Ordinary unlock verification never locks an already-unlocked collection first.
notes:

The approved product architecture now uses zbus plus GNOME's private org.gnome.keyring.InternalUnsupportedGuiltRiddenInterface to target any Secret Service collection by ID, so private-bus coverage is required and this ticket is promoted to P1/in-progress. Historical optionality remains true only for the older control-only architecture; preserve the existing control lifecycle as a sibling mode. Current slice stops after reusable broker/daemon/command lifecycle, ownership readiness, and a plain-session/private-interface smoke proof; it does not implement product zbus code or CLI behavior.

It composes systemd-socket-activate -> exec dbus-broker-launch --scope=system -> exact dbus-broker child with a minimal config; ListActivatableNames returns only org.freedesktop.DBus. Bounded readiness proves ListNames, exact launcher/broker executable and parent identities, shared listener inode at launcher FD 3/broker FD 6, daemon stdout/control readiness, and one owner for org.gnome.keyring + org.freedesktop.secrets whose Unix PID is the manually launched daemon. private_bus_probe.py opened a plain session and introspected InternalUnsupportedGuiltRiddenInterface plus unlock/change methods without calling a password method or changing lock state. Teardown directly reaps command/daemon/launcher and uses a pidfd to signal/observe the exact broker while requiring its launcher to reap it; TERM/deadline/KILL fallback is bounded and no broad kills are used. title: gmellon: headless GNOME keyring collection CLI
description: Provide headless password operations for any collection exposed by gnome-keyring-daemon. Use GNOME's private org.gnome.keyring.InternalUnsupportedGuiltRiddenInterface over D-Bus for collection-targeted unlock/change, while standard Secret Service APIs provide collection discovery, labels, aliases, and lock state. The earlier private control-socket path is login-only and remains historical/fallback research until the D-Bus backend is proven, after which obsolete product machinery should be retired deliberately. Full evolving spec lives in README.md.
acceptance_criteria: gmellon lists collection IDs and metadata, unlocks and changes the password of a selected existing collection without GUI prompting, defaults selection to login where appropriate, never relocks an already-unlocked collection unless an explicit side-effecting verification flag is requested, detects unsupported GNOME private API capability clearly, and passes isolated private-bus real-daemon tests with TTY/stdin-only secret input and documented exit behavior.
close_reason: Epic boundary complete: release security (encrypted session with monitor proof) and packaging/polish (status, -v diagnostics, completions with zimfw integration, help pass) landed; all product stages closed. Remaining children: gmell-firmament-config is deliberately deferred (P4, upstream under rebuild) and does not gate the epic. Publishing 0.1.0 to crates.io is now an operator decision, unblocked.

title: Store an SSH key passphrase, verified against the key
description:
gmellon ssh add KEY: prompt for the KEY's passphrase (TTY or --stdin, house contract; explicitly not the keyring password), verify it decrypts KEY, and only then store it the way gcr-ssh-agent will find it.

Verification without argv exposure (house policy forbids password argv): spawn ssh-keygen -y -f KEY with SSH_ASKPASS=<current exe>, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force, and a hidden __askpass helper subcommand that reads one line from stdin and prints it; the parent feeds the passphrase through a pipe. Two runs: the real passphrase must succeed, and a deliberately-wrong passphrase must fail (detects unencrypted keys, which have nothing to store). Neither condition holds -> refuse with an actionable message and store nothing.

Storage: CreateItem on the ReadAlias(default) collection (report the resolved ID), replace=true, attributes {unique: ssh-store:<absolute path>, xdg:schema: org.freedesktop.Secret.Generic}, label 'Unlock password for: <basename>'; the passphrase is sealed with the existing encrypted session machinery. Locked target collection is refused with a pointer to gmellon unlock.
acceptance_criteria: wrong passphrase stores nothing (exit 2); unencrypted key stores nothing (exit 1) with both ssh-keygen outcomes proven in the harness; correct passphrase stores exactly one item with the gcr-matching attributes (fixture-side decrypt proves the stored secret equals the passphrase); a new CreateItem body monitor proves the passphrase crosses the bus only as ciphertext; replace=true rotates an existing item rather than duplicating; full checks pass.
notes: 2026-09-14 complete. Askpass verification: SSH_ASKPASS=current exe + SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force + GMELLON_ASKPASS env marker selected in main() before parsing (ssh-keygen execs the askpass with the prompt as argv[1], not a subcommand); the helper reads one line byte-at-a-time (unbuffered so repeated execs share the pipe without over-reading) and prints it; two ssh-keygen -y runs (real + deliberately-wrong probe) decide Verified/Rejected/NotEncrypted. Generation of encrypted fixture keys cannot use askpass (generation prompts read piped stdin directly and buffered): a pure-Rust nix-pty generator with prompt-synchronized writes (tests/harness/common, no python dependency per operator). Storage: CreateItem(replace=true) sealed under the encrypted session, default-alias target (unset alias refused honestly - NoDefaultCollection; the harness fixture now sets the alias like a real desktop), gcr-matching unique + xdg:schema attributes (verified against gcr-ssh-agent-interaction.c), label 'Unlock password for: <basename>'. Proofs: refused store exits 2 with nothing stored, unencrypted key exits 1, verified store + replacing re-store with exactly two encrypted CreateItem bodies under the new body monitor, fixture GetSecret readback decrypts to the fed passphrase, ssh_verify integration suite (Verified/Rejected/NotEncrypted/empty/missing).
close_reason: Verified-before-store landed with no-argv discipline throughout (askpass for verification, pty for fixture generation): wrong passphrases and unencrypted keys store nothing, correct passphrases store exactly once replaceably in the gcr-visible default-alias collection with matching attributes, the passphrase crosses the bus only as ciphertext (CreateItem monitor), and the stored value round-trips through a gcr-style encrypted GetSecret readback. Full checks green.

title: gmellon: keyring item and SSH key management
description: Grow gmellon past collection-level operations into item management, with a gcr-ssh-agent-compatible SSH key passphrase layer. Grounding (verified against gcr 4.4 source): gcr-ssh-agent looks up key passphrases via libsecret with the generic schema (org.freedesktop.Secret.Generic, SECRET_SCHEMA_NONE), matching attributes unique=ssh-store:<absolute key path> plus the xdg:schema attribute libsecret writes for dotted schemas; lookup goes through secret_password_lookupv which searches the default-alias collection. Items are therefore stored with both attributes, in the collection resolved from the Secret Service ReadAlias(default) (normally login), labeled 'Unlock password for: <basename>'.
acceptance_criteria: Item-level read (list), gcr-compatible SSH passphrase store with verify-before-store, and SSH listing all land with private-broker proofs including a CreateItem body monitor proving the passphrase crosses the bus only as ciphertext; other collection commands keep their contracts; full check set passes.

title: Stage 2.5: secret input (TTY prompt + --stdin line)
description: Secret acquisition for unlock/change. TTY no-echo prompts via rpassword 7.5 on the controlling terminal (established local precedent: Atuin, tassle). Explicit --stdin path uses a small ordinary line-record reader behind an injectable BufRead seam, NOT rpassword's interactive editor, so piped control bytes (backspace, 0x7f, etc.) stay literal data. UTF-8 input contract: invalid UTF-8 errors rather than silently replacing; the control protocol itself stays raw-byte capable. Secret owns Zeroizing<String>, exposes as_bytes() only, no Debug/Clone/Display and no ownership escape. LF and CRLF terminate a line; EOF before newline errors; empty line passes through. Explicit bounded maximum input length so an untrusted pipe cannot drive unbounded allocation. TTY ENXIO (no controlling terminal) maps to an actionable error suggesting --stdin. Reusable two-prompt confirmation for Stage 4 change: single-shot mismatch error, both temporary values zeroized. Error values and messages never contain secret content.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests without a live TTY cover: LF termination, CRLF termination, empty line, invalid UTF-8 rejection, unterminated EOF error, at-limit acceptance, over-limit rejection, literal control bytes on the stdin path, matching and mismatching confirmation, ENXIO to actionable error mapping, and interop with control::sans_io encoding via Secret::as_bytes. rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, and nextest all clean. No public API leaks secret content through Debug/Display/Clone or by value.
notes:
Claimed for implementation. Architecture accepted from prior crate assessment: rpassword 7.5 for controlling-TTY no-echo prompts; explicit --stdin line-record reader behind injectable BufRead seam (pipes must not be interpreted by rpassword's interactive editor); UTF-8 input contract with error-not-replace; bounded input length; ENXIO -> actionable --stdin hint; reusable two-prompt confirmation.
Final shape: MAX_SECRET_BYTES = 64 KiB public const; read_stdin_line bounds buffering with reader.take(MAX+2).read_until so a never-terminating pipe cannot drive unbounded allocation; LF or CRLF terminate, lone CR is content, EOF-before-newline errors (empty pipe included), empty line yields empty secret, invalid UTF-8 errors via str::from_utf8 with no error path retaining bytes. prompt/prompt_confirmed wrap rpassword::prompt_password_with_config (controlling TTY); ENXIO from opening /dev/tty maps via classify_terminal_error to NoControllingTerminal suggesting --stdin. confirm_with(prompt, confirmation_prompt, impl FnMut(&str) -> Result<Secret, SecretError>) is the reusable Stage 4 core: single-shot mismatch, both temporaries zeroized on drop. Tests include the contrast test showing rpassword's configured reader edits piped control bytes while ours keeps them literal, plus sans_io encode/decode round-trips through Secret::as_bytes for ASCII and multibyte.
Post-review hardening commit 5cc5d988: stdin preallocates MAX_LINE_BYTES so secret prefixes cannot be abandoned by Vec reallocations; SecretError::Io retains only ErrorKind and numeric errno, discarding arbitrary reader text; TTY answers pass through the same 64 KiB limit while already inside Zeroizing<String>; public confirm_with was replaced by concrete read_stdin_confirmed and a private confirmation core; bounded-reader test now asserts logical consumption. README now scopes zeroization and rpassword terminal restoration as best-effort. Verified 54 nextest tests, 2 doctests, rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, and rustdoc -D warnings.
close_reason: Re-reviewed secret input now meets the bounded allocation, redacted error, shared size-limit, deep API, UTF-8, confirmation, and best-effort zeroization contracts.

title: Add synchronous control transport with async-ready seams
description: Build the synchronous Unix-socket adapter around the sans-I/O control codec. Keep framing and result parsing independent of I/O; keep path and peer validation usable with any AsFd socket; name the concrete adapter SyncClient so a future TokioClient can coexist without a generic async/sync trait. Each operation opens one daemon connection, validates the socket and peer UID, sends the credentials NUL followed by a zeroizing frame, reads the exact response under a timeout, and returns typed local/daemon outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: SyncClient exposes unlock and change; pure codec remains I/O-free; reusable Unix validation is not coupled to std::os::unix::net::UnixStream where AsFd suffices; fake Unix-server tests cover credential-byte ordering, UNLOCK and CHANGE exchange bytes, partial response delivery, missing/refused daemon, non-socket and symlink paths, peer validation, malformed/truncated responses, and bounded reads. No secret-bearing type implements Debug or leaks payloads. rustfmt, clippy, rustdoc, and nextest pass.
notes:
Implementation uses a sans-I/O protocol core plus an explicitly synchronous adapter. Future Tokio support should add a sibling adapter and reuse protocol + AsFd validation, not force async and sync through one trait.
Implemented as control::sans_io + Linux-only SyncClient + Metadata/AsFd Unix validation. Review corrections added an absolute response deadline resistant to drip-fed bytes, transport-level peer mismatch rejection before credential transmission, explicit Linux API gating, and proof that one client opens fresh connections. The timeout is documented as total response-read plus per-write, not an overall connect/exchange deadline. Standards review found no hard violations or code smells. Verified rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, and 28 nextest tests.
close_reason: Synchronous transport, async-ready seams, security validation, response deadline, typed errors, and complete fake-server coverage are implemented and reviewed.

title: Explore gmellon as an SSH_ASKPASS provider backed by the keyring
description: Exploratory: ship gmellon askpass (or a --askpass mode of the existing hidden helper) that answers passphrase prompts by looking up ssh-store items, so gcr-ssh-agent or ssh-add can pull straight from gmellon-managed storage. Security-sensitive: it would make gmellon a passphrase oracle for any process that can set SSH_ASKPASS; needs an explicit threat-model note and possibly per-key confirmation before adoption.
acceptance_criteria: Not committed for implementation. A design note in design/ evaluates the exposure and the gcr interaction contract before any code.
notes:
Committed to implementation (user decision 2026-09-17). Posture chosen: per-key opt-in attribute gmellon:askpass=allow, default-deny — plain gcr items are never answerable. Design note with the verified OpenSSH/gcr contract: design/askpass/askpass.glm53.md. Entry points: multicall gmellon-askpass + hidden __askpass subcommand; read path via GetSecret under the encrypted session (shared with future gmell-ssh-verify); CLI: ssh add --askpass, ssh allow/deny; ssh-list gains ASKPASS column.
Implementation landed 2026-09-17. Entry points: argv[0] multicall gmellon-askpass + pre-clap __askpass interception (clap_complete 4.6.5 generators advertise hidden subcommands — verified — so the interception keeps it out of help/completions entirely). Verified daemon finding recorded in the design note: gnome-keyring CreateItem-replace matches subset-on-new-fields, so a grant-carrying store duplicates an un-granted item; stores replace with the plain gcr attribute set then merge the grant via the writable attributes property. Private-broker CLI proof passes the full lifecycle (default-deny refusal, grant, answer x3 entry/prompt shapes, ssh-list/items columns, gcr-compat read, revoke, --askpass one-shot, removal) with redaction scans; stdout-exempt runner documented in the proof.

title: Re-verify stored key passphrases against their keys
description: gmellon ssh verify [KEY]: decrypt the stored passphrase (the one place gmellon reads a secret back) and check it still unlocks the key with the same askpass-based ssh-keygen verification. Catches key regeneration with a new passphrase leaving a stale stored secret. Reading secrets back is new product surface: the read path must decrypt under the encrypted session and keep the same zeroization discipline as input.
acceptance_criteria: verify reports per-key verdicts (match/stale/missing-key) without printing passphrases; stale detection proven in the harness by rotating a test key; the decrypted secret never appears in streams or artifacts (redaction scan); full checks pass.

title: Compose CLI configuration with Firmament
description: Adopt the local Firmament checkout at ../firmament (~/src/firmament), our figment2 fork, for gmellon's one-shot non-secret configuration. Introduce a config domain that keeps invocation concerns (selected subcommand and password source) separate from composable settings. Derive clap Parser, serde Serialize/Deserialize, and bon Builder on the appropriate configuration input type, using Firmament's Serialized and Env providers. Precedence must be CLI > GMELLON_-prefixed environment > application defaults. Feed resolved control/data path settings into later local-store and command wiring rather than reading process environment throughout the application. Passwords and other secret values must never enter Firmament, environment configuration, files, provenance, or Debug output. Use the stable one-shot composition API; do not pull Firmament ops/state/live machinery into this CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo uses the local ../firmament dependency in a way that makes the eventual publish dependency decision explicit; clap parsing remains user-friendly and subcommand semantics are not treated as persisted configuration; a typed resolved config is composed with CLI > GMELLON_ env > defaults and validates required values after extraction; absent optional CLI values do not overwrite lower providers; XDG fallback inputs remain distinguishable from explicit gmellon overrides; no secret field is representable in the configuration model; deterministic tests cover each precedence level, absent-value behavior, invalid values, and separation of command/input-source from settings; README documents supported environment keys and local-checkout/publishing implications; rustfmt, clippy, rustdoc, and nextest pass.
notes:
Implementation starts after the collection pivot. Scope is one non-secret setting, default_collection, composed as CLI override > GMELLON_DEFAULT_COLLECTION > login. Command selection and --stdin remain invocation-only and never enter Firmament. The local ../firmament path dependency will be documented as intentionally non-publishable until a registry/git dependency decision.
2026-09-12 architectural review: Firmament is under active rebuild and is not ready for gmellon adoption. The attempted one-setting integration was removed in commit 3b214ac0 because a configurable default collection does not justify configuration machinery and the local dependency complicates packaging. Keep this as lowest-priority future exploration only when multiple durable non-secret settings create a real configuration domain; do not block CLI work.
Status corrected from in-progress to deferred: no Firmament code remains in the working product, and no implementation is active while the upstream rebuild continues.

title: Stage 6 (stretch): explicit lock subcommand, login-hook docs
description:
Genuinely optional post-publish items. Two independent deliverables, no dependency on gmell-polish. If neither itches, drop the ticket without regret.

ITEM 1 - gmellon lock [COLLECTION] (explicit state change)
- Standard org.freedesktop.Secret.Service.Lock(ao collections) -> (ao locked, o prompt) via a new proxy method in src/secret_service/proxies.rs; reuses the existing collection resolution.
- Semantics: defaults to login like every other command; already-locked is success 0 without any call beyond the property read (mirrors AlreadyUnlocked symmetry); never invoked by any other command (the never-relock discipline runs both directions).
- Prompt policy, fail closed: gnome-keyring locks collections without a prompt (locking is free; unlocking is prompt-gated - the secret-tool asymmetry). Assert the collection appears in the returned locked list and the prompt path is empty/'/'; if a real Prompt object comes back, error with a clear message that interactive prompt objects are not performed, rather than implementing the org.freedesktop.Secret.Prompt loop. Keep the scope honest.
- No --all flag: document a list+loop one-liner instead if someone wants it.
- Proof (private broker): lock an unlocked collection and assert the locked property flips; siblings remain unlocked; already-locked returns 0; missing ID rejected before any Lock call; zero password-method calls observed by the interface-wide body monitor (locking never touches passwords); unlock-then-lock-then-unlock rotation works.
- Docs: README subcommand section + exit notes (existing table), status.md behavior section.

ITEM 2 - documented opt-in zsh login-hook pattern (docs only, no code)
- The elegant form needs no gating primitive: gmellon unlock on an already-unlocked collection exits 0 without reading a password (long-proven behavior - missing collections rejected before input, already-unlocked early return), so the hook is simply:

    # opt-in: prompt only when the login keyring is actually locked
    if [[ -o interactive ]] && (( $+commands[gmellon] )); then
      gmellon unlock
    fi

- First shell after login prompts; subsequent shells are silent no-ops. Wrong password exits 2 and the next shell retries. The interactive-guard keeps non-interactive shells (scp, CI, hooks) from touching rpassword, which already classifies no-TTY as an input error.
- Where it lives: README shell-integration section beside the zimfw module, with an explicit contrast - the zimfw module handles environment (never prompts on load); this hook handles unlocking (prompts only when locked, by explicit user choice). Cross-reference from zimfw/README.md. Footnote: once status lands in gmell-polish, a status-gated variant is possible, but the unconditional form is simpler and equally safe.
- Acceptance here is documentation review: the pattern never auto-prompts a non-interactive shell, and the claims it makes about already-unlocked behavior cite the existing proofs.
acceptance_criteria: lock uses the standard Service.Lock API, defaults to login, treats already-locked as success, is never called by other commands, and fails closed with a clear message if the daemon demands a Prompt object; its private-broker proof covers the lock flip, sibling isolation, already-locked success, missing-ID rejection, and zero password-method calls under the interface-wide body monitor; the login-hook pattern is documented as copy-paste opt-in zsh with the interactive guard, cross-referenced from the zimfw module README, and makes no claims beyond proven behavior; README and status.md updated; full check set passes.
notes: 2026-09-13 complete. lock: standard Service.Lock proxy method, LockOutcome::Locked/AlreadyLocked semantics (already-locked makes no Lock call), fail-closed LockPromptRequired/LockIncomplete error arms in the exit-1 family, default login. Private-broker proof: lock flip with sibling isolation, idempotent no-op, unlock-lock-unlock rotation, missing-ID rejection before any Lock call, exact wire counts (fixture locks + exactly 2 CLI locks; 13 unlock bodies; lock invocations contribute zero password-method calls - the interface-wide body scan covers the whole run). Login-hook pattern documented in README with the interactive guard and the proven already-unlocked-never-prompts justification, cross-referenced from zimfw/README.md. The obsolete INITIALIZE env-exposure item stays dropped. Checks: dev/harness/check all green, nextest 90/2 default and 117/4 login-control, clippy -D warnings all-features, fmt, doc, zsh suite 68/0.
